chunks: Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Muhammad ibn Salim, from Ahmad ibn al-Nadr, from Amr ibn Abi al-Miqdam who said:
I saw Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) and he was drinking from a ceramic cup.

key_terms.خَزَف: Ceramic, earthenware, or pottery — fired clay vessels
key_terms.قَدَح: A cup or bowl used for drinking, often of modest material

ai.seo_question: What type of cup did Imam al-Baqir use for drinking?
ai.summary: This hadith reports that Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (peace be upon him) was observed drinking from a ceramic (earthenware) cup. The narration serves as a record of the Imam's personal conduct and practice, establishing the permissibility of using ceramic vessels for drinking. In the context of early Islamic jurisprudence regarding the permissibility of various utensils, this direct eyewitness account from a companion of the Imam carries normative weight for Shia fiqh on household vessels.
